title: SF313 (2025-2026 Regular): Denial of the right of a person to purchase, own, possess, or carry a firearm solely on the basis that the person is enrolled as a patient in the medical cannabis registry prohibition

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction, 2025-01-16; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/94/2025/0/SF/313/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version as filed (SF 313, 2025, dated 2025-01-16). Ruled single: every part concerns gun eligibility; the registry-data limits apply only to gun approvals. Section 3 adds the quoted cannabis sentence; clause (10)(iii) already carries cannabis-use language in the text read.

operative_text:
Section 6 (Minn. Stat. 624.7153, new): A person may not be denied the right to purchase, own, possess, or carry a firearm solely on the basis that the person is a qualifying patient. A state or local agency may not access a database containing the identities of qualifying patients to obtain information for the purpose of approving or disapproving a person from purchasing, owning, possessing, or carrying a firearm. A state or local agency may not inquire about a person's status as a qualifying patient for the purpose of approving or disapproving the person from purchasing, owning, possessing, or carrying a firearm.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.713, subd. 1): Participation as a patient in the registry program under sections 152.22 to 152.37 or use of adult-use cannabis flower, adult-use cannabis products, lower-potency hemp edibles, or hemp-derived consumer products by a person 21 years of age or older does not disqualify the person from possessing firearms and ammunition under this section.
Section 4 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 6): A sheriff shall not deny an application for a permit to carry solely because the applicant is a patient enrolled in the registry program under sections 152.22 to 152.37 and uses medical cannabis flower or medical cannabinoid products for a qualifying medical condition or because the person is 21 years of age or older and uses adult-use cannabis flower, adult-use cannabis products, lower-potency hemp edibles, or hemp-derived consumer products.
Section 5 (Minn. Stat. 624.7142, subd. 1): (8) when the person is enrolled as a patient in the medical cannabis registry under sections 152.22 to 152.37, uses medical cannabis, and knows or has reason to know that the medical cannabis used by the person has the capacity to cause impairment.
